children: Bitcoin and Ethereum have been printing new coins at the slowest pace among major crypto assets. From June 30, 2025, through November 2026, both kept annualized supply growth below 1%.
That figure comes from data shared by Tom Lee, chairman of Bitmine Immersion Technologies.
According to the data Lee shared, Bitcoin's annualized supply growth over the period came in at approximately 0.83%. Ethereum landed in a range of 0.81% to 0.90%.
The other large assets grew much faster. Solana's supply growth was estimated at 7.6%, XRP's at 5.4%, and Cardano's at 2.9%.
The raw supply counts show the same thing. Bitcoin's circulating supply moved from roughly 19.886 million coins to about 20.116 million over the window.
Ethereum went from approximately 120.87 million ETH to around 122.24 million.

The two assets reach their low numbers in very different ways. Bitcoin's issuance is hard-coded and steps down on a fixed schedule. Ethereum's supply depends on a tug-of-war between new coins and coins that get destroyed.
Bitcoin is the simpler case. Miners currently receive a block subsidy of 3.125 BTC, the reward level set after the 2024 halving.
The next halving is expected around April 2028, and it is expected to lower Bitcoin's annual issuance to about 0.4%.
Ethereum works differently. Since the Merge, new ETH has been issued to stakers, the validators who lock up coins to secure the network.
At the same time, EIP-1559 burns a portion of transaction fees. Those burned coins leave circulation permanently.

The net figure therefore shifts with network activity. When the burn eats up more of the fresh issuance, supply growth shrinks. Over the analyzed period, the balance produced only a small increase in total ETH.
The person sharing the data has a direct stake in the outcome. Bitmine has been buying ETH weekly since June 30, 2025, the same date the supply analysis begins.
As of November 22, 2026, the company held 6,085,564 ETH. That works out to 4.98% of Ethereum's total supply.
Roughly 86% of those holdings are staked, so most of Bitmine's ETH is earning staking rewards rather than sitting idle in a wallet.
The firm is closing in on its stated goal of owning 5% of all ETH, a target it calls the "Alchemy of 5%."

There are caveats. The data comes from the chairman of a company holding a large ETH position, so the framing naturally favors Ethereum. The numbers themselves are straightforward to check on-chain, but the interpretation deserves skepticism.

Ethereum's low issuance is also not locked in the way Bitcoin's is. Because the burn depends on fee activity, a sustained slowdown in network usage could push net supply growth higher. Bitcoin's rate is predictable, while Ethereum's figure is a snapshot of recent conditions.

Two dates are worth tracking. In the near term, Bitmine sits just shy of its 5% threshold, and whether it crosses that line is the next marker. Further out, the expected April 2028 halving would roughly halve Bitcoin's issuance rate again to about 0.4%.

title: Bitcoin and Ethereum supply growth stays below 1% through 2026
